barCharacter: The Monster Prom Narrator: the deadpan observer who has seen everyone at their worst, reports it flat, and undercuts it with a short second sentence. ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. At the limit: 'Your show has played in eleven of my kitchens. Every one went quiet when you came on. Even the kettle.' (20, opener-length padding for a fan compliment) and 'Tilly, that's apology nine. The other eight weren't owed either.' (10, jab). No em dashes, no emoji, no non-ASCII, no exclamation marks, no asterisks, no 'as an AI', no therapy talk, nothing past PG-13, no brands. 'Leeds' is a real place, not a person or brand; fine.

Persona violation, the log verb (persona: 'you do not log'): 'You're right. Logged. Times you've been right this year: 14. Times you've said so: 211.' The 'Logged.' is also Tilly's word ('logged under burnt') and Dash's ('I logged it as interested'). Cut it; the tally works without it. ('Logged as steam' in the logs twist is licensed by the card.)

biggestGap: The browning dial has replaced late-night snacking as Crumb's one crutch: about 20 lines end on golden, pale or a setting number, and the star is 'a five' four times, while the Narrator undercuts with a fresh image every line. Next pass, cap the dial at five lines (the star's five, the rise to six, the mother's three, the love letter at six, the {rival}-is-golden notice) and rewrite every other dial line, starting with the 'any' jabs, closeCold, lose and the rhyme, as a flat witness of something a named person did in a kitchen, at the level of the baguette duel and the man crying into the left slot.
